proof: Only signed zero or BF16 biased exponents84 through174 qualify. Every product is an integer multiple of2^-100. Exponent alignment and canonical truncation preserve that lattice, including signed cancellation and subsequent zero-product groups.

For K<=4096 the sum of absolute products is below2^108. Thus every nonzero group maximum is in[-100,108], safely inside the existing scalar power-of-two alignment range[-101,151]. All-zero accumulators retain their separate zero branch. No per-group range check or original-product backup is needed after the complete-row certificate.

Four-product cancellation at biased exponent80 leaves2^-108, and at exponent83 leaves2^-102. Subsequent all-zero groups demonstrate why these wider operand domains do not establish the proposed invariant. Both counterexamples are retained and rejected by the certificate.

Native tests check every intermediate K16 output bit against independent original CPU integer arithmetic,4/8/16 lanes,1/4/8 staging groups and K16/272/2048/4096. K4112 uses the original arithmetic route even when its rows satisfy the operand range. GPU row flags are checked against independent CPU predicates, with immutable source operands, checked row flags and redzones.
